issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters StockIngredient(String, int, int), and the reference solution implements such a three-argument constructor. However, the template's StockIngredient class only provides a four-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This constructor-parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from instantiating StockIngredient using the expected three-argument form (e.g., new StockIngredient("Bacon", 10, 50)) as shown in the problem text and commented Main examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template (or provide an overload that delegates to the existing constructor) so that the template matches the problem specification and the example usages. Ensure the constructor behavior matches the solution's validation/initialization rules.

issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository defines only a four-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This API/identifier mismatch (extra boolean parameter) creates confusion for students implementing SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery or instantiating StockIngredient using the three-argument form shown in the problem and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the StockIngredient API consistent: add or restore a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template (or provide an overloaded three-arg constructor delegating to the existing one). This aligns the template with the problem UML and the solution implementation and avoids forcing students to supply an unrelated boolean parameter.
